While visiting in Pennsylvania I experienced the only major hallucination I've ever had. Well, it must be a hallucination. I hope it was a hallucination. I hear voices, but they are all the Dragon, or versions of me (for the most part at least). Occasionally I will see bugs, rodents, shadows, eyes in the dark, animals racing out of the brush toward the wheels of my car. This was totally different.

 

I was lying awake in the guest bedroom of an associate of mine. The whole house was dark save for a beam of moonlight that shot down the hallway from a warped plastic window blind that was a couple of inches out of place. There was a shuffling sound in the hallway, like feet, and then it abruptly stopped. I was watching the door, curious but not afraid; there were cats living there, I figured it was one of them trotting around in the dark. A few seconds later there was a soft tap, and then a subtle scraping, like a fingernail trailing down the wall. The sound was getting closer to my door, and now I was afraid.

 

I stared at the doorway, eyes straining in the dark, and then the doorway was full. There was a tall man in the door, wearing a long black coat that covered everything but the tips of his feet. He had a black hat with a wide brim that was tilted down at an angle, concealing his face. It was too insane, it had to be shadows, it had to be something. I kept blinking, but every time my eyes opened he was still standing there. I couldn't move, or scream, or even breathe, I just sat and stared at the shape in the doorway. Then it moved. He tilted his head up in a sort of inquisitive pose, and his skin was white, whiter than bone, white like nothing natural, and his eyes were shining like a cat's eyes do in the dark. Then he smiled at me, sunnily, innocently, and his mouth glittered with rust and razor blades and chips of glass. I opened my mouth to scream, but I couldn't form a word, or make a sound, everything was dry. He closed his mouth, and brought one impossibly long finger to his lips and made an insectile hissing sound that I think now was an instruction, "Shhhhhhhhh". Then he walked down the hall, toward the room where all my children slept; rats in cages and cats sleeping on papasan chairs. I heard his coat swishing, then the snick of a door closing. That thing was in there with my kids, he was going to bite them, and eat them. The spell broke, the paralysis fell away. I leapt from the bed, raced into the hall, slamming hysterically into the wall. Down the hall the door was closed, HE had closed it, and I hit it with my shoulder while scrambling for the knob and fell in. Other than my startled half asleep kids, it was empty. The closet was a walk-in type, and the door was open just a crack. I kicked on the lights and flung the door open. There was nothing remarkable.

 

I spent the rest of the night nailing the closets shut, and left at sunup with my kids, a suitcase and no words of explanation or goodbye. I've never seen him again, perhaps because there are no closets in hotels.
